Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

unusual adjective

also uncommon, out of the ordinary, unusually, it’s unusual for

classical

Caes. B.C. 3.47: nova et inūsitāta bellī ratiō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Deiot. 1: inūsitātum est with a clause

inūsitātus, inūsitāta, inūsitātum

adjective, declension

unusual, uncommon, extraordinary

The negative of ūsitātus (see normal).

Other words

  • īnsolitus, īnsolita, īnsolitum — unaccustomed; unusual

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.361: īnsolita mihi loquācitās (Lewis & Short); Plin. Pan. 60.6: rārum ac prope īnsolitum est

    Of people it means “unaccustomed to” (īnsolitus ad labōrem, Caes. B.C. 3.85); of things, “unusual”.

Examples

  • nova et inūsitāta bellī ratiō

    a new and unusual way of making warCaes. B.C. 3.47 (Lewis & Short)

  • in prīncipe rārum ac prope īnsolitum est, ut sē putet obligātum

    in a ruler it is rare and almost unheard of to think himself under an obligationPlin. Pan. 60.6 (Lewis & Short)

  • Inūsitātum est tē tam mātūrē surgere.

    It’s unusual for you to get up so early.composed

See also normal.

SourcesLewis & Short: inusitatus · Lewis & Short: insolitus

Caesar, Cicero and Pliny quoted as Lewis & Short quotes them.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
